gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's 350 W kit panel is listed at 33 V open-circuit (Voc) while the Elite 200 V2, Elite 300 and Elite 400 take only 12–60 V on their solar input. Two of these panels in series reach about 66 V or more, so every '2 × 350 W' BLUETTI kit has to be wired in parallel. Anker's F3000, by contrast, has a separate 11–165 V high-PV port that BLUETTI says takes four 400 W panels in series.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited; read 2026-11-17). It already gives the voltage and current window for many stations, checks series and parallel wiring for EcoFlow's 2 × 220 W and BLUETTI's 2 × 200 W kits, and warns that cold raises panel voltage. So the method is on a cited page, but it does not list any 350 W BLUETTI kit, any panel figures for the 350 W or SORA 500, or the F3000's port voltages (it says only '2,400 W dual-voltage solar'). solargenadvisor.com, theoutageready.com and dealectric.com would not load through the fetch tool (self-signed certificate error), so I could not check them for this point.
decides: This confirms rather than changes the pick. The '2 × 350 W' kits (Elite 200 V2 at $2,040.60, Elite 400 at $2,325.60, Apex 300 at $2,469.05 link price) still work, but only with the two panels in parallel, because series would exceed the 60 V input on Elite-series stations. The kit box BLUETTI lists has no parallel (Y-branch) cable, so the page should say in the kit's row to check whether one is included and to wire in parallel. On a page about future solar growth this favours the Anker F3000, which has a 165 V port for a series string, over the single-input BLUETTI Elite kits. It does not move the value or ships-now pick.

findings.product: BLUETTI 350W Solar Panel (the panel in the BLUETTI '+350W' kits)
findings.label: Open-circuit voltage (Voc)
findings.note: The page text says '33V open-circuit voltage (Voc)'. Its Tech Specs table is empty, so Isc, Vmp and Imp are not on the page. Two in series = 2 × 33 V = 66 V before any cold-weather rise, which is above the 60 V ceiling of the Elite 200 V2, 300 and 400. BLUETTI's older PV350 manual is reported at 46.5 V Voc (see unsourced), which would be 93 V in series. Either way, series is over the limit.

unsourced: Vmp, Imp and Isc of BLUETTI's US 350 W kit panel. Its US page has an empty spec table. A search snippet says it lists 46.5 V Voc, 10.8 A Isc, 37.5 V Vmp and 9.2 A Imp; that figure is not confirmed. Without Imp I cannot show whether two panels in parallel stay under the Elite 200 V2/400's 20 A input.
